text: In the Beginner project, Carraway Supply Co.'s Sales Director asked one question, you answered it with a one-time pull, and that was that. This time, the ask grows. Two stakeholders want a piece of the same data, every single week, and neither one wants a one-off.

The Sales Director wants an executive summary: total sales, average order value, a trend line, refreshed automatically before every Monday leadership meeting, with no more asking you to re-run anything. The Operations Manager wants something very different from the same data: a page she can filter and slice herself, down to specific regions and product lines, to spot where orders are piling up or shipping late.

Everything in this chapter still comes from the real AdventureWorks2012 database, nothing invented. Sales dot SalesOrderHeader holds one row per order. Sales dot SalesOrderDetail holds one row per order line, with the product and the line total. SalesTerritory gives you region names. Product and ProductSubcategory give the Operations Manager something real to drill into.

Here's why recurring changes the build, not just the schedule. The query logic has to be staged once and reused every refresh, not retyped. Power BI has to refresh on its own schedule in the Service, not wait for you to republish by hand. And with two pages pulling different cuts of the same numbers, you need real tables with real relationships behind them, not one flat query result pasted into a single visual.

One more honest note before you start: this project includes a real bug on purpose. Later, after both pages are built and published, two visuals that are supposed to show the same number won't agree, and you'll diagnose exactly why. Next lesson: planning the architecture that makes all of this possible before you write a single line of SQL.
